daily_brief: Youth-led protests over the cost of living and underfunded public services swept across Europe this weekend, with demonstrations turning violent in both France and Germany. More than 320,000 people marched in France [RFI], while German police deployed water cannons in Frankfurt, Berlin, and other cities after clashes broke out [BBC]. Meanwhile, diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the U.S.-Iran conflict continued in Doha, with President Trump stating the U.S. still has 'one or two targets' to address in Iran while expressing openness to negotiations [The Hindu], [Globe and Mail]. In a significant humanitarian development, hundreds of Ukrainian civilians were evacuated from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky following a local ceasefire brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump [BBC]. Cryptocurrency exchange Binance announced it has covered 90% of the $6.3 billion stolen in what the FBI confirmed was a North Korean-backed hack [BBC], [Globe and Mail]. Senegal made history by hosting the first Olympic event on African soil as the Youth Olympic Games opened in Dakar [France 24], [RFI].

top_stories.headline: Youth-Led Cost of Living Protests Turn Violent Across France and Germany
bullets: More than 320,000 protesters marched across France on Saturday, with 70,000 in Paris; police made over 290 arrests after clashes erupted at the end of demonstrations

In Germany, tens of thousands joined protests organized by 'Gen Z regelt' in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne, and Hamburg; police used water cannons after rioters targeted emergency workers and looted shops
Protesters demanded action on underfunded schools, high living costs, public spending cuts, and opposed military service
German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt called for 'harsh punishments' for rioters and said police prevented violence similar to recent Paris unrest

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Focused on violence and police response in Germany, noting protests followed similar French demonstrations

top_stories.headline: Trump Signals Possible Iran Strikes After Midterms as Diplomatic Talks Continue in Doha
bullets: President Trump stated the U.S. has 'one or two targets' remaining in Iran, specifically mentioning 'Pickaxe Mountain,' a suspected underground nuclear complex
Iranian negotiators held talks with Qatari mediators in Doha on Saturday following 12 hours of discussions in Tehran on Friday
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump has not decided on new strikes and prefers diplomatic resolution
Iran's Supreme Leader ordered armed forces to prepare for 'immediate, impactful, and geographically unrestricted' response to any attacks

sources.framing_note: Detailed Trump's comments about remaining targets and Iran's denials of nuclear work at the site

top_stories.headline: Hundreds of Ukrainians Evacuated from Russian-Occupied Oleshky After Melania Trump-Brokered Ceasefire
bullets: Hundreds of residents were evacuated from the front-line city of Oleshky on Friday, crossing from Belarus into Ukraine's Chernihiv region on Saturday
Evacuees had been trapped for years without adequate food, water, or electricity; some resorted to cooking garden weeds to survive
President Zelensky thanked U.S. First Lady Melania Trump for brokering the local ceasefire that enabled the evacuation
Emotional family reunions occurred at the arrival site, with some elderly evacuees so weak they were carried on stretchers

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Multiple articles provided detailed human interest coverage of evacuees' experiences and family reunions

top_stories.headline: Binance Covers 90% of $6.3 Billion Hack Losses as FBI Confirms North Korean Responsibility
bullets: Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, stated it has replenished 90% of assets stolen in Thursday's hack using company funds
The FBI confirmed North Korean state-sponsored unit TraderTraitor (Lazarus Group) was responsible for the attack
Hackers were observed converting stolen assets to Ethereum, with further laundering expected through decentralized finance services
Withdrawals have been partially restored after being suspended following the breach

sources.name: BBC
sources.framing_note: Focused on company's response and FBI attribution to North Korea

sources.name: Globe and Mail
sources.framing_note: Emphasized this was a record heist and included CEO's direct quotes about covering user losses

top_stories.headline: Youth Olympic Games Open in Senegal, Marking First Olympic Event on African Soil
bullets: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye declared the fourth Summer Youth Olympic Games open at Diamniadio Olympic Stadium near Dakar
The opening ceremony featured hundreds of drummers and dancers celebrating Senegalese and African culture under the motto 'Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates'
Nearly 3,000 athletes aged 14-17 from over 200 countries will compete across three Senegalese cities in 25 sports
The Games come amid an economic crisis in Senegal and a government crackdown on LGBTQ+ people

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Noted economic context and LGBTQ+ crackdown alongside celebration of historic event

sources.name: RFI
sources.framing_note: Emphasized the ceremony as a symbol of African unity and cultural diversity
